order: Build the alias layer and the roster kill switch, before any rename. Declare in router/aliases.json every 6.6 retired name -> (role, rung) pair alongside the legacy identity it keeps while the old roster is installed, each with its ledger deprecation line. Have router.resolveSeat() evaluate the roster flag PER ORDER ('legacy' -> the installed legacy agent unchanged; 'new' -> the casting tables through the degradation machine), with the declarative default at 'legacy' as the kill-switch home position — rollback is a flag flip, no reload. Load the map under the same fail-closed discipline the other tables get: an unknown role, a rung the named role does not have, a missing legacy identity, or a bad roster default must each refuse construction. Prove it: an order written against old names dispatches correctly under both flag values, with the flip demonstrated mid-session on one router instance; executor-heavy-xhigh is Principal's routed xhigh effort point, not a second seat; detective is the merged Investigator with the read-only pin carried; reviewer and reviewer-codex resolve to the computed Reviewer, never a static casting; every retired-name resolution emits its deprecation line under both flags; and a tampered alias map fails the load closed.
claims: Every item of the order is delivered. router/aliases.json declares all 16 retired names with their new (role, rung) pair, the legacy identity each keeps, and its ledger deprecation line; router.resolveSeat() reads the roster flag per order and falls back to the declarative rosterDefault ('legacy'), so rollback is a flag flip on a live router with no reload. The map is loaded under the same fail-closed discipline as castings.json and charters.json: an unknown role, a rung the named role does not have, a missing or unknown-model legacy identity, and a bad rosterDefault each refuse construction. Verification: tests/router.test.js section 12 covers the order item by item, and the suite is green at 93 passed / 0 failed. The section's closing check writes a tampered copy of aliases.json to a temp dir with executor.new.rung set to a rung Builder does not have, hands it to createRouter({ aliasesFile }), and asserts construction throws with the "does not have" refusal — the tampered map fails the load closed. The flip is exercised mid-session on a single router instance (alternating roster values across successive resolveSeat calls); executor-heavy-xhigh lands on Principal's routed xhigh effort point rather than a second seat; detective carries the read-only pin onto the merged Investigator; reviewer and reviewer-codex both come back as the computed Reviewer, not a static casting; and all 16 retired names emit their deprecation line under both flag values.
